title: A Play To Be Bused Out Of

contact_edits.before: The only good moments come when the play settles for public address as public address, instead of trying to pass it off as dialogue: when Dan Chameroy's nervous prof makes his doomed presentation to the Board of Education, or when, in the most powerful performance of the evening, Kevin Hanchard's assembly-line worker makes his rejoinder. The setting consists of fairly basic projections (pop groups and other memorabilia), and the costumes change to reflect the passage of time; as often happens in such cases, much of the acting is done by the hairstyles. This seems fitting for a play whose idea of establishing period is to have someone say, "We've got a new album. It's that Broadway musical Hair." - Palmer Park plays in repertory at the Stratford Shakespeare Festival until Sept. 21. For tickets and information, call 1-800-567-1600, or visit stratfordfestival.com.
